title: Rational character filtrations and coaction subquotients
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G$ an affine $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Use the actual finite rational coordinate comodules and comodule maps of [def-sfb-rational-representation-gzero], and coordinate Hopf algebras, character elements, stable subspaces and simplicity of [def-sfb-rational-highest-weight-data]. For two rational modules $(V,c_V),(W,c_W)$, say that $V$ is a rational subquotient of $W$ if there is a coaction-stable subspace $N\subset W$, its restricted coaction $d$ characterized by $(\iota\otimes1)d=c_W\iota$, and a surjective linear map $q:N\to V$ satisfying $(q\otimes1)d=c_Vq$. For a character $\chi:G\to\mathbf G_m$ define its actual coaction on $F$ by $a\mapsto a\otimes\chi$, where $\chi$ denotes the pullback of the Laurent coordinate. This map is counital and coassociative: these two properties are the named proof obligations of the character module. Define $F_\chi$ by this map on the actual space $F$. A character filtration of a finite rational module $M$ is an integer $r\ge0$, an increasing sequence of actual subspaces $M_j$ indexed by $j\ge0$ with $M_0=0$ and $M_r=M$, and all $M_j$ coaction-stable; for each $0\le j<r$ it specifies a character $\chi_j$ and a surjection $q_j:M_{j+1}\to F$ with kernel $M_j$, commuting with the restricted coaction and the character coaction. The restricted coactions are pinned by their inclusions. This defines the data, without asserting that a filtration exists.
